In response to growing public opinion opposing conscription, beginning in 2021, South Korea will begin a plan to eventually phase out the active conscription program and replace it with a voluntary service system.

Over the first year, the length of service will be reduced to 15 months for all branches of the military, down from 21-24 months. Conscientious objectors will, for the first time, be allowed to opt for civil service duties lasting 24 months instead of being convicted and imprisoned. In order to incentivize volunteering, the Military Manpower Administration will reimburse enlistees' college education following completion of the standard service of 21-24 months.

In 2022 service will be again reduced to 12 months for active duty and 15 months for conscientious objectors.

In 2025, the conscription system will begin using a lottery system that conscripts only 50% of the male population coming of age (20 years old). Each year the percentage will be reduced by 10% and by 2030, the conscription system will be placed on standby. At this point all males will still be required to register with the Military Manpower Administration in the event of an emergency draft being required.
